t: Blocks COX-1 and COX-2, so fewer prostaglandins are made
Blocks β1-adrenergic receptors in the heart (slower rate, less force)
Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, so less angiotensin II
Blocks angiotensin II at its AT1 receptor
Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the key enzyme in cholesterol synthesis
Blocks the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the loop of Henle
Blocks the Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal tubule
Irreversibly blocks the H⁺/K⁺-ATPase in stomach parietal cells
Blocks histamine H2 receptors on parietal cells
Blocks the serotonin transporter (SERT), so more serotonin stays in the synapse
Makes GABA-A chloride channels open more often
Blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway
Binds penicillin-binding proteins and stops bacterial cell wall cross-linking
Binds the bacterial 50S ribosome and blocks protein synthesis
Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
Activates μ-opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord
Blocks voltage-gated Na⁺ channels in nerve fibres, locally
Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, so fewer clotting factors are made
Blocks the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor
Stimulates β2 receptors and relaxes airway smooth muscle
Blocks muscarinic receptors in the airways
Crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted into dopamine
Activates 5-HT1B/1D receptors (constricts meningeal vessels, less CGRP release)
Blocks L-type calcium channels in arterial smooth muscle
Lowers glucose output from the liver and improves insulin sensitivity
Blocks SGLT2 glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule
Blocks influenza neuraminidase so new viruses can't be released
Binds ergosterol and punches pores in fungal membranes
Inhibits xanthine oxidase, so less uric acid is made
Inhibits Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase in heart muscle (more calcium, stronger beat)
Blocks voltage-gated Na⁺ channels in neurons to stop seizure spread
Blocks nicotinic receptors at the neuromuscular junction (used in surgery)
Binds glucocorticoid receptors and switches off inflammatory genes
